selected_sources.reason: Official USGS documentation for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater flow model executed by the independent synthetic-truth generator.
Official USGS user guide for MODPATH 7, the particle-tracking model executed by the independent synthetic-truth generator.
Official USGS documentation for PHREEQC, whose thermodynamic direction bounds are retained by both hydrochemical panels in the reaction-family bootstrap.
Primary methodological example of combining multiple environmental age tracers (including 39Ar) to constrain groundwater age, supporting the rationale for a multi-tracer local age likelihood.
Primary methodological source on known limitations of environmental-tracer age inference, motivating explicit uncertainty propagation in the local age likelihood.

Cited only by analogy for the ESS >= 400 stability convention used across chains in rank-normalised MCMC diagnostics; this paper does not itself address single-particle-set importance-sampling effective sample size, and the Methods text now states this limitation explicitly rather than presenting the citation as direct endorsement.
Original source of the importance-weighting effective-sample-size formula (ESS as the reciprocal sum of squared normalised weights) used directly in this study's topology-conditioned age inference.

Primary methodological reference showing how precision-recall curves can provide a more informative view under class imbalance and relating ROC and PR spaces; it is not cited as an unconditional ranking of scalar AUC summaries.
Origin of the Brier score used jointly with log loss and expected calibration error to check that reduced uncertainty is not accepted without a calibration check.
Primary example of the conventional joint-inversion motivation for evidence integration, against which this benchmark's falsifiable decision-rule framing is contrasted.
Primary reference for treating multiple candidate models/evidence sources jointly under uncertainty, relevant background for the conventional integration rationale being tested.
Primary information-fusion treatment of sheaves as local data and consistency structures, supporting the global-section interpretation.
Primary mathematical source for cellular sheaf Laplacians, restriction maps and global sections.
Primary source explicitly relating scalar identity-restriction sheaf Laplacians to weighted graph Laplacians and motivating the identity-limit gate.
Recent non-peer-reviewed evidence that strong identity-sheaf baselines can be competitive in graph learning; used only to motivate comparator discipline, not as groundwater validation.
